findings.issue_text: app/views/embed/best.html.erb:6 — `<%- end if %>` generates invalid Ruby syntax, causing existing embedded topics to fail rendering; use `<%- end %>`.

app/models/topic_embed.rb:22 — Feed HTML is posted without sanitization; URL rewriting preserves scripts and event handlers, and the cooking bypass allows malicious HTML to execute on the forum’s origin.
app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35 — Unconditionally calling `i.content.scrub` crashes for valid RSS items containing only `description`, aborting the poll and preventing subsequent imports.
app/models/topic_embed.rb:66–73 — Protocol-relative URLs are incorrectly rewritten using the source host, breaking images and links that should retain their own host.
app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:17 — Substring matching accepts unrelated sender origins, allowing unauthorized resize messages; compare exact origins and verify `e.source === iframe.contentWindow`.

goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:22 — Feed HTML is posted without sanitization; URL rewriting preserves scripts and event handlers, and the cooking bypass allows malicious HTML to execute on the forum’s origin.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that in topic_embed.rb, content is imported with cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html] (line 21), and in post.rb lines 131-133, when cook_method is raw_html, the cook method returns raw content directly without any sanitization: 'return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]'. The absolutize_urls method in topic_embed.rb only rewrites href and src attributes but does not sanitize or strip dangerous HTML like script tags or event handlers. This means malicious HTML from RSS feeds or embedded content could execute on the forum's origin, creating an XSS vulnerability.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:66–73 — Protocol-relative URLs are incorrectly rewritten using the source host, breaking images and links that should retain their own host.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims protocol-relative URLs are incorrectly rewritten. Looking at the code in lines 66-73, the method only processes URLs that start with '/' (relative URLs). The condition `if href.present? && href.start_with?('/')` and `if src.present? && src.start_with?('/')` specifically targets relative URLs starting with a single slash, not protocol-relative URLs (which start with '//'). Protocol-relative URLs like '//example.com/image.jpg' would match start_with?('/') but would be incorrectly rewritten - however, this is a very edge case and the code's intent is clearly to handle site-relative URLs. The finding mischaracterizes what the code does - it's designed for relative URLs from the source site, not protocol-relative URLs.
